Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran internal numbers and have a rough monthly token profile that is lumpy for the first 6 months while we onboard several products. Procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a per-token ladder that has a short "fence" for overage smoothing and an explicit bridge clause to avoid punitive step-ups during onboarding.

Key ask: can you propose a structure that avoids big effective rate jumps in month 1-3 as usage spikes, while keeping unit economics predictable long term. We expect a run rate around 120B tokens/month by Q4, but months 1-3 might jump between 15B and 80B.

Attached is our rough forecast (BridgeHealth_usage_estimates_2028.xlsx). Procurement is sensitive to invoice volatility and wants a true-up window and a mechanism for limited crediting or temporary temporary uplift at the lower effective rate.

Can your side share two concrete options: one that is finance-friendly (easy billing, clear blended math) and one that is operations-friendly (marginal breakpoints but protective bridge).

Thanks,

Alex,

Really appreciate the forecast. High level we can do two defensible patterns:

1) Blended ladder with onboarding credit band (finance friendly)
   - Effective blended rate for the month calculated across all tokens; a short term onboarding credit offsets the first 30 days of overage above a baseline.
   - True-up quarterly with a 45 day settlement window.

2) Marginal breakpoints + soft bridge (ops friendly)
   - Marginal price tiers apply as you hit breakpoints. For the first 90 days from go-live, a soft bridge applies: if month X exceeds baseline by more than 40%, we temporarily apply the lower marginal rate up to a band equal to 25% of estimated monthly volume. Overages beyond that billed at regular marginal rates.

Quick pros/cons:
- Blended is simpler for invoice reconciliation and procurement but can hide marginal economics for engineering.
- Marginal + bridge preserves per-token incentives and lets you predict marginal cost, but requires agreed banding and a short true-up window to reconcile credits.

I'm attaching a short writeup with numerical examples (redwood-volume-fence-examples.pdf). Can you confirm which accounting org will sign or if a PO will be the preferred instrument? Also tell us the billing cadence you prefer (monthly vs monthly + 30 day provisional).

If you want, we can turn option 2 into a pilot: 90 day bridge band, 25% provisional volume cushion, quarterly true-up. Ben, can you check the math on the cushion sizing versus our expected SLA capacity?

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Option A — Blended Simple (procurement friendly)
- Calculate monthly blended effective rate across all tokens.
- Apply a one-time onboarding credit equal to 30% of overage above baseline for the first month only.
- Monthly invoice, single line item: "Redwood API usage (blended)".
- Quarterly true-up, 45 day settlement.

Option B — Marginal + Soft Bridge (engineering friendly)
- Marginal tiers apply by breakpoint.
- For onboarding first 90 days, apply a soft bridge: up to 25% of estimated monthly volume is billed at the lower marginal tier; any usage beyond that is billed at marginal rates.
- Monthly invoice lists a single gross line with an attached addendum showing tiered math. Quarterly true-up reconciles any provisional cushion usage.

Example numbers attached. My recommendation is Option B but present both. If procurement objects to provisional items on invoices we can simplify Option B to produce a single line by applying the provisional cushion as a pre-billed credit in the following invoice.

Ben, PT to you to sanity check the impact on committed capacity. Laura, if legal wants, we should surface the non-gaming clause and a 90 day lookback.
